text: Geranium maculatum seeds seem to respond to drying out by going dormant. If they are allowed to dry our and then are treated as C(30) or C(60), they do not have high germination rates. If they are processed and then kept moist (for instance in moist sand) in normal temperatures, they then respond very well to C(30) stratification. If they are dried out and later scarified (30 seconds to 2 minutes of rubbing between two pieces of sand paper) then seem to respond very well to C(30) conditions. Local Ann Arbor nurseries have offered this description.
